text.p: Shares in Swiss beer and mineral water group Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann Holding (FHH) were suspended from trading on the Swiss Exchange, but trading would resume around 1300 GMT, a bourse spokesman said.
Shares in Sibra Holding AG, in which FHH owns a majority, were also suspended from trading.
FHH, which was created recently through a merger of Feldschloesschen and Huerlimann, plans to merge with Sibra as part of restructuring of its share structure.
FHH said at a news conference that it planned to split its bearer shares and then swap them into registered shares during the first half of 1997.
FHH's share capital will also be raised to 49 million Swiss francs nominal from around 46 million.

Following the merger with Sibra, FHH said its share capital would consist of 1,528,902 registered shares, each with a 25 franc par value, and 1,109,450 participation certificates with a par value of 10 francs.

FHH also told the news conference that it did not expect profits for the 1995/96 financial year, which ends September 30, to reach last year's result as sales of brand items had fallen and profits would be burdened by extraordinary charges.
FHH also plans to concentrate its beer production in Rheinfelden and Sion with production in Zurich and Freiburg transferred to Rheinfelden.
The Gurten brewery will be closed by the end of this year.
The restructuring will lead to the cut of some 680 of 3,500 jobs in Berne, Zurich and Fribourg, FHH added.
Write-downs and provisions from the restructuring amount to around 315 million and will be fully charged to the 1995/96 accounts.
FHH expects the moves to lead to a cost reduction of around 60 million francs from 1998/99 year.
Gerard Stalder, previous general director of Schenk Holding, will become chief executive of FHH from November 1.
